title: Proverbs, Chapter 18 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 18 on folios 415v, 416r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 18 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 415v, 416r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>לְֽ֭תַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ נִפְרָ֑ד בְּכָל־תּ֝וּשִׁיָּ֗ה יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃ <sup>2</sup>לֹֽא־יַחְפֹּ֣ץ כְּ֭סִיל בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה כִּ֝֗י אִֽם־בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת לִבּֽוֹ׃ <sup>3</sup>בְּֽבוֹא־רָ֭שָׁע בָּ֣א גַם־בּ֑וּז וְֽעִם־קָל֥וֹן חֶרְפָּֽה׃ <sup>4</sup>מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים דִּבְרֵ֣י פִי־אִ֑ישׁ נַ֥חַל נֹ֝בֵ֗עַ מְק֣וֹר חָכְמָֽה׃ <sup>5</sup>שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא־ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃ <sup>6</sup>שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃ <sup>7</sup>פִּֽי־כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה־ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ <sup>8</sup>דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Through desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh and intermeddleth with all wisdom. <sup>2</sup>A fool hath no delight in understanding, but that his heart may discover itself. <sup>3</sup>When the wicked cometh, then cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach. <sup>4</sup>The words of a man's mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook. <sup>5</sup>It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to overthrow the righteous in judgment. <sup>6</sup>A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes. <sup>7</sup>A fool's mouth is his destruction, and his lips are the snare of his soul. <sup>8</sup>The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>גַּ֭ם מִתְרַפֶּ֣ה בִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא לְבַ֣עַל מַשְׁחִֽית׃ <sup>10</sup>מִגְדַּל־עֹ֭ז שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בּֽוֹ־יָר֖וּץ צַדִּ֣יק וְנִשְׂגָּֽב׃ <sup>11</sup>ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ וּכְחוֹמָ֥ה נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ׃ <sup>12</sup>לִפְנֵי־שֶׁ֭בֶר יִגְבַּ֣הּ לֵב־אִ֑ישׁ וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוֽ͏ָה׃ <sup>13</sup>מֵשִׁ֣יב דָּ֭בָר בְּטֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִוֶּ֥לֶת הִיא־ל֝֗וֹ וּכְלִמָּֽה׃ <sup>14</sup>רֽוּחַ־אִ֭ישׁ יְכַלְכֵּ֣ל מַחֲלֵ֑הוּ וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה מִ֣י יִשָּׂאֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>15</sup>לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יִקְנֶה־דָּ֑עַת וְאֹ֥זֶן חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תְּבַקֶּשׁ־דָּֽעַת׃ <sup>16</sup>מַתָּ֣ן אָ֭דָם יַרְחִ֣יב ל֑וֹ וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְדֹלִ֣ים יַנְחֶֽנּוּ׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>He also that is slothful in his work is brother to him that is a great waster. <sup>10</sup>The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe. <sup>11</sup>The rich man's wealth is his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit. <sup>12</sup>Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility. <sup>13</sup>He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him. <sup>14</sup>The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear? <sup>15</sup>The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge. <sup>16</sup>A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ יבא־ [וּבָֽא־] רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ׃ <sup>18</sup>מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד׃ <sup>19</sup>אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת־עֹ֑ז ומדונים [וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים] כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן׃ <sup>20</sup>מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע׃ <sup>21</sup>מָ֣וֶת וְ֭חַיִּים בְּיַד־לָשׁ֑וֹן וְ֝אֹהֲבֶ֗יהָ יֹאכַ֥ל פִּרְיָֽהּ׃ <sup>22</sup>מָצָ֣א אִ֭שָּׁה מָ֣צָא ט֑וֹב וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃ <sup>23</sup>תַּחֲנוּנִ֥ים יְדַבֶּר־רָ֑שׁ וְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר יַעֲנֶ֥ה עַזּֽוֹת׃ <sup>24</sup>אִ֣ישׁ רֵ֭עִים לְהִתְרֹעֵ֑עַ וְיֵ֥שׁ אֹ֝הֵ֗ב דָּבֵ֥ק מֵאָֽח׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him. <sup>18</sup>The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty. <sup>19</sup>A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle. <sup>20</sup>A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; and with the increase of his lips shall he be filled. <sup>21</sup>Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof. <sup>22</sup>Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD. <sup>23</sup>The poor useth intreaties; but the rich answereth roughly. <sup>24</sup>A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
